change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admins who are not owners are refused by the permission check
findings.body: The check at lines 46-48 joins `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, and the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. `isTeamAdmin` returns the membership for role ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284), and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER (lines 286-295). The conjunction therefore reduces to `isTeamOwner`, so a team ADMIN who is not the owner gets FORBIDDEN at line 55. The existing UI treats admin-or-owner as the rule (BookingListItem.tsx:546, `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`). Fix: use `isTeamAdmin` alone, which already covers OWNER, or `||` with awaits if both are kept.
findings.originReason: The handler file is new in this diff.

verification.reason: isTeamAdmin matches ADMIN or OWNER and isTeamOwner matches OWNER only. Joining them with && reduces the check to owner-only, so a non-owner ADMIN who is neither organizer nor attendee gets FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: Guest blacklist is bypassed by mixed-case addresses
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased when read (line 71), but each guest is compared as typed (line 77: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A guest entered as `Spam@Example.com` passes when the env list contains `spam@example.com`, and the address is then stored as an attendee and emailed. The sibling check lowercases both sides (packages/trpc/server/routers/publicViewer/checkIfUserEmailVerificationRequired.handler.ts:16-17). Fix: compare `guest.toLowerCase()`.

verification.reason: The blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is compared as typed, so a mixed-case address passes the filter. The sibling handler lowercases both sides.

findings.title: Duplicate guests in one request create duplicate attendees and invites
findings.body: The server never deduplicates `guests`. The uniqueness rule exists only in the dialog (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29), and the schema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) is just `z.array(z.string().email())`. `uniqueGuests` (lines 74-78) filters only against existing attendees, and `createMany` (lines 100-103) then writes every row. The Attendee model has only `@@index([email])` and `@@index([bookingId])` with no unique constraint (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:526-539), so the same address is stored twice and emailed twice. The same issue affects the email split: email-manager.ts:541 classifies recipients with `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` over the raw input, so a resubmitted existing attendee receives the 'booking scheduled' email, not the add-guests email. Fix: dedupe `uniqueGuests` (case-insensitively) before creating attendees and pass the deduped list to the email call.

verification.reason: The server schema is a plain email array and uniqueGuests only filters out existing attendees, so a duplicate inside one request is written twice by createMany (Attendee has no unique constraint). The email split also checks the raw `guests` list, so a resubmitted existing attendee gets AttendeeScheduledEmail.

findings.title: Calendar update result is discarded; the mutation reports success and the retry path is blocked
findings.body: Guests are written to the database (lines 92-106) before the calendar is updated, and `updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without looking at its outcome (line 165). `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` returns void (packages/core/EventManager.ts:596-602) and drops the per-calendar results that `updateAllCalendarEvents` builds and returns (EventManager.ts:920). The sibling `editLocation` handler checks those results and writes or sends only on success (editLocation.handler.ts:107-126). With the add-guests code, if a calendar update fails the user still gets 'Guests added', the emails go out, and the organizer's calendar event does not list the new guests. A retry is then refused with BAD_REQUEST, because the guests are now attendees and are filtered out at lines 74-81, so the calendar update cannot be re-run from this UI. Fix: check the results and surface a failure, or do the calendar update before the database write, matching editLocation.

verification.reason: updateCalendarAttendees returns void and drops the updateAllCalendarEvents results, while the attendees are already written to the database. A failed calendar update is therefore invisible, and a retry hits BAD_REQUEST because those guests are now attendees. editLocation checks the results before writing.

findings.title: Email failures are logged without the error
findings.body: The catch at lines 169-171 declares `err` and never uses it, so the log line 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' carries no cause. The handler still returns 'Guests added'. The sibling in editLocation.handler.ts:139-141 has the same shape, so this matches existing practice. Logging the error object (through `logger.error`) would make the failure diagnosable.

verification.reason: `err` is caught and never logged, so the log line carries no cause. The same pattern exists in editLocation, so this is minor.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore the event type's 'disable standard emails' settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no event type metadata and sends to the organizer, team members and attendees unconditionally. Its siblings gate on the event type: `sendLocationChangeEmails` checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (email-manager.ts:495-521, helpers at lines 81-87), and `editLocation` passes `booking.eventType.metadata` (editLocation.handler.ts:135-138). The add-guests handler calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` without metadata (addGuests.handler.ts:168), so an event type that disables host or attendee standard emails still emails them about new guests. Fix: accept `eventTypeMetadata` and apply the same two gates, passing `booking.eventType?.metadata` from the handler.
findings.originReason: New function added by this diff.

verification.reason: sendAddGuestsEmails takes no metadata and sends organizer, team and attendee emails unconditionally. The sibling sendLocationChangeEmails gates on eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail.

findings.title: Organizer add-guests email ignores EMAIL_FROM_NAME
findings.body: The From display name uses `APP_NAME` (line 23; import at line 1). Sibling organizer emails use `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`, e.g. organizer-location-change-email.ts:23 and organizer-scheduled-email.ts:47. `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` is `process.env.EMAIL_FROM_NAME || APP_NAME` (packages/lib/constants.ts:31). A self-hosted instance that sets EMAIL_FROM_NAME gets a different sender name on this one email. Fix: import and use `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`.

verification.reason: The new template uses APP_NAME for the From display name, while the sibling it was copied from (organizer-location-change-email) uses EMAIL_FROM_NAME.

findings.title: Permission error uses a translation key that does not exist
findings.body: The FORBIDDEN message is `you_do_not_have_permission` (line 55). That key is absent from apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json; the only permission key there is `dont_have_permission` (common.json:1628). The dialog renders `t(err.message)` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43), so the user sees the raw string 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'. Fix: use `dont_have_permission`, or add the key.

verification.reason: en/common.json has no `you_do_not_have_permission` key; only `dont_have_permission` exists. The dialog calls t(err.message), so the raw key is shown.

findings.title: Stale 'emails must be unique and valid' message survives a successful add and a close
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true in `handleAdd` (line 56) but is reset only by the Cancel button (line 91). The success path (lines 36-41) clears the emails and closes the dialog but leaves `isInvalidEmail` set. Closing with Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange`, line 61) also leaves it set. The component stays mounted for each booking row (BookingListItem.tsx:357-361), so on the next open the red error appears before the user has typed anything. Fix: reset `isInvalidEmail` in `onSuccess` and in the `onOpenChange` handler. Closing through Escape also keeps the typed emails, while Cancel clears them (lines 89-93); the two close paths should behave the same.

verification.reason: isInvalidEmail is reset only by the Cancel button. onSuccess and onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} leave it set, and AddGuestsDialog stays mounted in each BookingListItem, so the error persists to the next open.

findings.title: Error fallback can never run; a raw message is shown for non-tRPC errors
findings.body: `message` is a template string, so it is always truthy and `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` (line 44) is dead code. For errors without a tRPC `data`, `t(err.message)` shows the raw message. Build the string conditionally, or use the fallback only when `err.data` is absent.

verification.reason: `message` is a non-empty template literal (it contains at least ': '), so it is always truthy and the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip in a component that otherwise translates
findings.body: The remove-button tooltip is the literal 'Remove email' (line 46), while the rest of the component uses `t()` (lines 13, 69). It will show English in every locale. Use a translation key such as `t('remove_email')`, or reuse an existing key.

verification.reason: The tooltip content is the literal 'Remove email', while the same component uses t() for its other strings.

findings.title: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary recipients who receive platform mail
findings.body: `isAttendee` (lines 52-54) lets any attendee whose session email matches add any addresses. The platform then sends them invitations: AttendeeAddGuestsEmail sets `from` to the organizer's display name (packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:20), and there is no rate limit or cap. Is this intended? If the product wants only the organizer, team admins or owner to add guests, the attendee branch should go. If it is intended, a per-booking cap or a rate limit would limit abuse. I could not find a rule in the repository that answers this.

verification.reason: Factually true: any attendee whose session email matches passes the check and can add arbitrary addresses. Those addresses get AttendeeScheduledEmail invitations, and existing attendees get AttendeeAddGuestsEmail sent under the organizer's display name. There is no cap. Whether this is intended is a product question, so consider fits better than fix.

findings.title: No booking-status check: cancelled, rejected or past bookings accept guests
findings.body: The lookup (lines 26-42) does not filter by status or time, and the handler never checks either. The UI only shows the action for non-cancelled bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:544-554), but the API accepts any `bookingId`, so guests can be added to a cancelled or rejected booking and invited to it. Decide whether that should be rejected server-side.

verification.reason: The booking lookup filters only by id, and the handler never checks status or time, so cancelled or rejected bookings accept guests through the API.

findings.title: Misleading error when every requested guest is already an attendee or blacklisted
findings.body: Lines 80-81 throw BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' when `uniqueGuests` is empty. That also happens when the guests are already attendees or are on the blacklist, so the user is told the emails are not unique or valid when they are. A distinct message would help the user.

verification.reason: An empty uniqueGuests, which also happens when every guest is an existing attendee or blacklisted, throws the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'.

findings.title: No tests for the new handler or the dialog
findings.body: The pull request adds no test file. The permission branch (line 46), the blacklist (line 77), the duplicate handling (line 74) and the email split (email-manager.ts:541) are all untested. The bugs above would be caught by handler tests covering a team admin, a non-owner, a mixed-case blacklisted address and a duplicate in one request.

verification.reason: Searching for *ddGuest* finds only the handler, schema, templates and dialog, with no test files for the new handler or dialog.

contracts.action: Open the 'Add guests' dialog from the Edit menu
contracts.before_after: The sibling 'Edit location' action sets a dialog flag and renders EditLocationDialog. The new action sets its own flag and renders AddGuestsDialog (BookingListItem.tsx:357-361). Both live in the same editBookingActions list, so the same visibility rules apply (BookingListItem.tsx:549, 553-554).
contracts.visible_effect: A dialog opens with one blank email field and an 'Add' button.

contracts.action: Call trpc viewer.bookings.addGuests from the dialog
contracts.before_after: editLocation uses bookingsProcedure, which allows the organizer or a collective member and throws UNAUTHORIZED otherwise (util.ts:19-65). Its handler wraps all work in try/catch and rethrows INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (editLocation.handler.ts:31, 143-145). addGuests uses authedProcedure and performs its own permission check (addGuests.handler.ts:46-56), which contains the && bug above. There is no try/catch.
contracts.visible_effect: onSuccess shows 'Guests added' and invalidates the list. onError shows 'CODE: message' and does not invalidate.
contracts.failure_mode: Any throw after the database write (line 92) leaves the guests stored, shows an error, and keeps the list stale; see the calendar finding at addGuests.handler.ts:165.

contracts.action: Persist guests, then update the calendar
contracts.before_after: editLocation updates the calendar first, checks the results, and writes the booking only when at least one result succeeds. addGuests writes attendees first and then awaits a void calendar call that drops its results.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees success while the calendar may not list the new guests.
contracts.failure_mode: Guests are stored without a calendar update and without emails. A retry is refused at lines 74-81 because they are now attendees.

contracts.action: Send add-guests emails after the handler returns
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/editLocation.handler.ts:134-141 (sendLocationChangeEmails, gated by event type metadata in packages/emails/email-manager.ts:495-521)
contracts.before_after: The sibling passes the event type metadata, so the event type's disable flags apply. The add-guests call passes no metadata, so they do not apply.
contracts.visible_effect: Emails go to the organizer, team members and every attendee, and the user sees 'Guests added' regardless.
contracts.failure_mode: A thrown error is caught and logged without its cause, and success is still returned (lines 169-171).

contracts.action: Close the dialog and reopen it after a validation error or a success
contracts.before_after: Cancel clears the emails and the error flag. Success clears the emails but not the error flag. Escape and overlay close clear neither.
contracts.visible_effect: The red 'Emails must be unique and valid' text appears again on the next open, before anything is typed.

contracts.before_after: The sibling uses EMAIL_FROM_NAME. The new email uses APP_NAME, which ignores the EMAIL_FROM_NAME override.
contracts.visible_effect: The sender display name differs from the other organizer emails on instances that set EMAIL_FROM_NAME.

contracts.action: Remove an email row with the addon control
contracts.visible_effect: The row is removed. The button has no handler of its own, so the click reaches the addon wrapper's onClick, which calls onClickAddon.

contracts.before_after: Same pattern as the existing AddressInput lazy wrapper.
contracts.visible_effect: Nothing renders until the chunk loads.

summary: Reviewed the 15 files in this part (no build or test runs). Main defects: the team-admin permission check uses && and so refuses admins who are not owners (addGuests.handler.ts:46); the guest blacklist is case-sensitive, so mixed-case addresses bypass it (addGuests.handler.ts:77); duplicate guests in one request create duplicate attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:74); the calendar update result is discarded, so a failed calendar update still reports success and blocks a retry (addGuests.handler.ts:165); add-guests emails ignore the event type's disable-standard-emails settings (email-manager.ts:525); the organizer email ignores EMAIL_FROM_NAME (organizer-add-guests-email.ts:23); the FORBIDDEN message uses a translation key missing from en/common.json (addGuests.handler.ts:55); and the dialog keeps a stale validation error after success or close (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36). I also raised one question for the author: whether any booking attendee should be able to add arbitrary recipients who then receive platform mail with the organizer's name (addGuests.handler.ts:52). The pull request adds no tests. The emails are registered in the template index, so renderEmail resolves them. The attendee permission question and the status-check question are the only items I could not settle from the code alone.
